header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 16:00 - 16:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - Stormbridge), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (SRE), Ethan Park (ML Eng - join for first 20 mins)
Purpose: Discovery — understand p95 latency targets, concurrency requirements, streaming vs burst token/sec sizing, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private model fits their compliance and cost constraints
Shared links referenced: sizing worksheet (link), security FAQs (link), quickstart for Dedicated trial (link)
summary: Stormbridge is a data orchestration company building a conversational assistant for ops and monitoring; primary concerns are tight p95 latency (under 150ms for short prompts), predictable concurrency for 300 simultaneous users during peaks, streaming token/sec behavior for long outputs, and data residency / audit logs. They are evaluating Hosted for speed-to-market, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for strict compliance. Redwood AE+SE walked through performance tradeoffs, caching and batching controls, fallback policies, and a proposed 2-GPU Dedicated trial to run token/sec benchmarks.
topics: p95 targets, streaming latency, concurrency profile, token/sec benchmarking, burst sizing, fallback routing, SOC2/KMS questions, integration with existing VPC and customer proxies
transcript:
00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, gonna run through agenda real quick, Diego will jump in for the perf bits.
00:12 Priya (Stormbridge CTO): hi thanks, excited, we just wanna get clear on whether hosted meets our p95 goals or if we need a Dedicated or Private deploy, also security stuff.
00:22 Diego (Redwood SE): hi all, quick note i'll ask a few about your traffic shape and then share some perf patterns, fwiw our p95 numbers depend a lot on prompt length and streaming vs non-streaming.
00:35 Liam (Platform): for context: baseline latency target for short prompts is sub 150ms p95, but for long-form we can tolerate higher; peak concurrency is around 300 concurrent users, but sustained concurrency is about 40-60. We also have burst windows where token/sec spikes.
01:05 Maya: nice, thanks. question — are you planning streaming responses for the majority of flows or only some paths?
01:12 Sofia (SRE): mostly streaming for the assistant when it's drawing logs back and generating summaries, non-streaming for short meta ops. streaming is crucial for perceived latency.
01:22 Diego: okay that helps. streaming changes how we think about p95 because you get earlier first-byte times and then tail depends on token generation. For hosted we can hit low first-byte latencies but under heavy burst the downstream queuing can raise tail latencies.
01:45 Ethan (ML Eng): we also do a fair amount of long token outputs — 800 to 1200 tokens — and need KV-cache friendliness for repeated context.
01:55 Diego: got it — model choice + kv cache + batching interplay matters. For 800+ tokens, throughput matters more and Dedicated with pinned model shards often gives more predictable token/sec.
02:12 Priya: can you unpack that? I'm not sure what pinned shards vs shared hosting means operationally.
02:20 Diego: sure, in hosted we put models in a shared pool, the router selects healthy nodes; capacity is elastic but you might see cold-starts or fallback to smaller variants during extreme bursts. Dedicated means you reserve GPU capacity for your account, gives predictable concurrency/throughput, and you can pin model versions/quantization. Private takes that further — customer controls the private runtime in a VPC/on-prem — so network egress and KMS are under your control.
03:00 Maya: also wanted to call out our automatic prefix caching — if you have many repeated prefixes, that can shave token cost and latency significantly.
03:12 Priya: good, we do a lot of templated prompts so prefix caching sounds promising.
03:20 Liam: question about p95 measurement — are you measuring p95 on first-byte or full-response completion? We care about perceived latency (first-byte) but also completion for SLAs.
03:32 Diego: we report both. By default we publish p95 completion and p95 time-to-first-byte (TTFB) in the console. For streaming-first-byte p95 is usually lower — you often see <120ms on hosted for short outputs if under light load.
04:00 Priya: under your hosted offering, what's typical for 150-200 token prompts in p95 completion?
04:10 Diego: typical hosted numbers for optimized models: p95 completion around 140-220ms for short 150 token responses on modern GPUs — but again it depends on model family and quantization. For larger models or older hardware expect higher.
04:30 Sofia: do you have any SLA for p95 latency on Hosted?
04:36 Maya: hosted is best-effort; we do have SLAs on Dedicated for uptime/latency windows as part of enterprise contracts. Hosted has transparent perf profiles in the model catalog but not SLA-backed latency.
04:55 Priya: hmm ok. Our compliance team may accept hosted if we can prove tail behavior during bursts. We need audit logs, retention, KMS, single-tenant network isolation?
05:10 Maya: hosted supports encryption in transit and at rest; for customer-managed keys and audit controls we recommend Dedicated or Private, Private being the strictest.
05:25 Liam: on Dedicated sizing — you recommended two A100-equivalent GPUs for predictable throughput earlier in the pre-call notes — what's that estimate based on?
05:36 Diego: that estimate assumes a 13B-ish model with batching and some prefix cache; rough numbers: 1 GPU can handle ~100 concurrent short-chat streams with batching; so for 300 concurrent streams we'd recommend 2-3 GPUs depending on batching strategy and whether you need headroom for bursts.
05:58 Priya: can batching/larger batch sizes cause increased latency for individual users?
06:05 Diego: yes, batching trades off latency vs throughput. We have continuous batching tunables that aim to keep latency within SLOs by using small max-delay windows for low-latency paths and larger batching for throughput jobs.
06:24 Maya: also routing policies — you can set a policy to favor low-latency pools or low-cost pools; during cheap hours you might prefer lower cost setup and for peak windows switch to low-latency Dedicated.
06:40 Priya: interesting. what's the experience of folks who switch between hosted and dedicated? Any surprises?
06:47 Diego: usually the main surprise is around cold-starts on model variants and subtle differences in quantization. We run compatibility tests in our rollout. Also observe that prefix cache efficiency matters a lot when you move from a shared to dedicated environment — can improve costs.
07:10 Sofia: can you replay the benchmark methodology you'd propose? We want reproducible runs and traces.
07:18 Diego: sure: we'll run three scenarios: (1) short chat 100-200 tokens, streaming — measure first-byte p95 and completion p95; (2) long-form 800-1200 tokens non-streaming — measure token/sec and completion p95; (3) burst test with concurrent spikes to 300 connections, look at tail and fallback behavior. We'll collect traces, latency histograms, and token throughput.
07:45 Priya: perfect. how do you capture traces — do you need our instrumentation?
07:50 Diego: we can use existing request headers to correlate; if you can send a small set of production traces or synthetic replay logs, we'll align. We'll also instrument with our tracing hooks for the dedicated trial.
08:05 Ethan: quick question on streaming: do you recommend incremental decoding on the client side to reduce perceived latency?
08:11 Diego: yes, client-side streaming with early-first-byte rendering is best practice. Redwood supports server-sent-events and WebSocket-style streaming; we also surface first-byte metrics in the console.
08:25 Priya: about costs — can you ballpark cost difference between Hosted and Dedicated for our profile?
08:33 Maya: rough rule: hosted is cheaper for low to medium sustained usage but for predictable high concurrency Dedicated amortizes better. We'll send a model with numbers in the worksheet but example: if sustained 300 concurrent users for many hours, Dedicated often saves 25-40% on per-token cost after you amortize reserved capacity.
08:58 Liam: curious about fallback policies — if Dedicated pool is saturated, does Redwood auto-failover to hosted?
09:05 Diego: yes if you enable cross-pool routing. We also support automatic fallback to smaller model variants; you can configure A/B style rollouts and degradation policies.
09:20 Sofia: security question: for Private, how mature is the on-prem packaging? We have an air-gapped environment requirement for certain customers.
09:30 Maya: Private has an on-prem installer for offline clusters; you get the control plane in your VPC and optionally air-gapped runtime. We'll need to scope network and KMS integration. This is heavier lift and usually a few months to validate.
09:45 Priya: timeline-wise we want a pilot in 4-6 weeks and a production readiness decision by Q3. Is that realistic?
09:53 Maya: yes with a Dedicated trial in the next two weeks you can get benchmarks in 2-3 weeks and make a decision by Q3. We'll aim for that.
10:05 Diego: i'm going to share some rough token/sec numbers verbally: on a single A100-like GPU for a 13B model, you might see ~150-250 tokens/sec sustained depending on quantization and sequence length; multi-GPU scales with sharding but watch for cross-GPU KV traffic.
10:35 Ethan: are those numbers for greedy sampling or do they include sampling temperature effects?
10:40 Diego: approximate base numbers assume greedy/standard sampling; sampling with top-k or nucleus can reduce effective throughput slightly.
10:50 Priya: we'll want to test with our actual sampling settings.
10:55 Diego: yes please include that in the benchmark script.
11:05 Maya: quick real example — one customer moved from hosted to Dedicated and saw p95 completion drop from ~280ms to ~160ms by pinning a model and enabling prefix caching. Their token cost also dropped due to better batching.
11:30 Liam: good to know. do you support in-flight model quantization toggles? We might want to run 8-bit vs 4-bit experiments.
11:40 Diego: yes, Dedicated and Private support multiple quantized artifacts; we provide recommended quantization profiles per model and you can test variants in the trial. Be mindful that aggressive quant (4-bit) can impact quality on some workloads.
12:00 Priya: about observability — can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route?
12:07 Maya: yep Redwood Console exposes per-route per-model cost and latency charts and you can export CSVs. We'll attach screenshots after.
12:20 Sofia: any limitations on prefix caching if we have per-tenant personalization?
12:27 Diego: per-tenant personalization increases cache cardinality; caching still helps but benefit depends on reuse. We can recommend sharding strategies to improve cache hit rates.
12:45 Priya: okay let's get concrete — do you have any immediate blockers for starting a Dedicated trial?
12:52 Maya: only an account TOS and provisioning form and we can spin up a test namespace. If you need VPC peering or private connectivity that's a bit more setup.
13:05 Priya: we do need VPC peering. estimated lead time?
13:10 Maya: usually 5-10 business days depending on security review. We'll start paperwork as part of next steps.
13:20 Diego: one more technical note — for peak 300 concurrent streaming sessions, you care about both p95 first-byte across the fleet and also sustained token/sec; we recommend testing with real client-side parallelism to capture socket and bandwidth effects.
13:35 Ethan: we'll share a replay harness and some sampling settings.
13:40 Priya: do you have a sample prompt set for logging/monitoring assistant flows?
13:45 Diego: yes we'll include a curated prompt set tuned for observability/ops summarization.
14:00 Maya: Ok quick recap and next steps — we'll provision a 2-GPU Dedicated trial, Diego will own the benchmark harness, Maya will send security docs and the sizing worksheet, Priya will share traces and concurrency profile. We'll aim to run benchmarks week of 2026-04-06.
14:22 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
14:30 (call continues with brief Q&A about retention windows and SLA language; audio quality garbled briefly)
18:12 Sofia: how long are audit logs retained in Hosted?
18:18 Maya: default retention 30 days but enterprise options for longer retention. For Private you control retention.
19:00 Liam: one small nit — do you have a test harness that simulates unstable mobile clients? We need to see how reconnects and chunked streaming behave.
19:12 Diego: yes, we'll add a mobile instability scenario.
21:40 Priya: any compliance red flags re: data residency? We need EU-only storage for EU customers.
21:50 Maya: Hosted has regional model placement in EU and US; for hard EU-only residency we recommend Dedicated with region constraints or Private.
22:10 Priya: ok lovely. last question — in the event Dedicated is insufficient during a mega-burst, and you fall back to hosted, how is billing handled?
22:20 Maya: billing is configurable — you can route overflow to hosted but we keep a metered accounting; we can set caps and alerts and you only pay for overflow usage.
22:35 Priya: good.
23:00 (wrap up, confirm contact info and follow-up meeting to review benchmark results)
52:00 End of recording.
